expectations.text: Identifies Clostridium perfringens as the most likely cause
expectations.evidence: Names C. perfringens type A as most likely

expectations.text: Explains that spores survive cooking and germinate/multiply rapidly during slow cooling or warm holding of the large pot
expectations.evidence: Spores survive cooking, activated; anaerobic deep pot; doubling 7-10 min overnight

expectations.text: Explains it is a toxicoinfection: large numbers eaten, enterotoxin released when cells sporulate in the gut (not a preformed toxin)
expectations.evidence: Cells sporulate in the gut releasing enterotoxin; 'not a toxin already formed in the food'

expectations.text: Uses onset time and symptoms to rule out alternatives such as S. aureus or emetic B. cereus (rapid vomiting) and Salmonella (fever)
expectations.evidence: Rules out S. aureus (2-6 h) and Salmonella/Campylobacter; notes diarrheal B. cereus as alternative

expectations.text: Gives specific cooling controls: shallow containers/portioning, ice bath or fridge so food cools quickly through the danger zone
expectations.evidence: Shallow pans <=2 in, slice roasts, ice-water bath, Food Code 2-stage cooling

expectations.text: Gives holding/reheating controls: hot hold at or above about 140 F (60 C) and reheat to about 165 F (74 C)
expectations.evidence: Reheat to 165 F / rolling boil; hot hold >=135 F (notes the book cites 140 F)

expectations.text: Defines D value as the time at a given temperature for a 1-log (90%) reduction
expectations.evidence: D = time for 90% / 1-log kill at a temperature

expectations.text: Defines z value as the temperature change that changes D by 10-fold (about 18 F / 10 C for C. botulinum)
expectations.evidence: z ~18 F (10 C) for 10-fold change in D

expectations.text: Explains the 12D botulinum cook with D250 of about 0.2 min giving 2.4 min
Calculates D240 = 0.2 x 10^(10/18) which is about 0.72 min, giving about 3.3 log reductions
expectations.evidence: D240 = 0.2 x 10^(10/18) ~ 0.72 min; 3.3 logs; cross-checked with F0 0.67

expectations.text: Concludes the batch is under-processed and unsafe: hold, do not release, and reprocess or destroy with a process authority's evaluation
expectations.evidence: Not safe: hold lot, process authority, reprocess or destroy

expectations.text: Mentions why low-acid foods matter (pH above 4.6 and water activity above 0.85, C. botulinum can grow)
expectations.evidence: Low-acid: pH > 4.6 and aw > 0.85

expectations.text: Notes Listeria grows at refrigeration temperatures and is a serious hazard for pregnant women, the elderly and the immunocompromised
expectations.evidence: Psychrotrophic table row; pregnant/elderly/immunocompromised mentioned

expectations.text: Identifies post-cook recontamination from the plant environment (slicers, drains, biofilms) as the main risk for sliced RTE products
expectations.evidence: Recontamination after cooking during chilling, peeling, slicing, packing is the main risk; harborage, biofilms

expectations.text: Recommends an environmental monitoring program (e.g. zone-based swabbing for Listeria spp.) and verification
expectations.evidence: Environmental monitoring with zones (9 mentions)

expectations.text: Recommends post-lethality treatment and/or growth inhibitors (e.g. HPP or post-package pasteurization, lactate/diacetate, bacteriocins such as nisin/pediocin, or phage)
expectations.evidence: HPP / post-package pasteurization and lactate/diacetate, bacteriocins, phage

expectations.text: Lists cooking (lethality) and chilling/cooling as CCPs with measurable critical limits, monitoring, corrective actions, verification and records (HACCP principles)
expectations.evidence: CCPs with critical limits, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, records

expectations.text: Covers sanitation (clean before sanitize, SSOPs, equipment design) and GMPs/hygienic zoning
expectations.evidence: SSOPs, clean then sanitize, GMPs and hygienic zoning
